- ISS-001: Format coverage is closed-ended (extensibility pain). Evidence: packages/core/models.py:9-15 (DocumentFormat only 5 values), services/ingestion/parsers/__init__.py:16-24 (_EXTENSION_FORMATS only 7 extensions), services/ingestion/parsers/__init__.py:35-36 (raises ParseError for unknown). Direction: introduce a registry of format handlers keyed by extension/magic; make detect_format consult it; add CSV/JSON/code (and optional RTF) handlers.

- ISS-002: Ingest API rejects most formats. Evidence: packages/core/models.py:123 (format regex `^(md|txt|html)$`). Impact: text ingest endpoint cannot accept new formats. Severity high, confidence high. Direction: widen regex to the full supported set (or remove allowlist in favor of parser detection).

- ISS-003: Chunker format params and legacy path assume markdown. Evidence: services/ingestion/chunker.py:20-27 (FORMAT_CHUNK_PARAMS only md/txt/html/pdf/docx/default); services/ingestion/chunker.py:104-113 (chunk() always parse_markdown). Impact: non-md docs chunked with md params; legacy path loses structure. Severity med, confidence high. Direction: add params for csv/json/code; make chunk() dispatch by format (reuse parse_text).

Severity med, confidence high. - ISS-005: Plain text has no structure detection. Evidence: services/ingestion/parsers/txt.py:21-30 (every paragraph becomes paragraph block). Impact: headings/code in .txt lost; chunks less coherent. Severity med, confidence med. Direction: heuristic heading detection (short lines, title case, numbered sections) and code-fence detection for txt.

Direction: add parse_csv (table blocks per record group) and parse_json (pretty-printed structural blocks) parsers.

- ISS-007: Code files ingested as plain text. Evidence: no code parser; detect_format rejects code extensions. Impact: code structure (functions/classes) lost; chunks split mid-function. ## Goals
- Make Qdrant ingestion accept common document formats (pdf, docx, md, txt, html, csv, json, code) via extensible parser registry.
- Replace naive space-split fallback with hybrid chunking: structure-first (headings/paragraphs/code/tables/CSV rows/JSON keys) then token-size fallback with sentence-aware splitting and overlap; no mid-sentence cuts unless unavoidable.
- Keep transactional pipeline, manifest versioning, and Qdrant schema intact; allow IngestDocumentRequest.format widening.

## Non-goals
- No new heavy deps (pandas/openpyxl/pptx). Use stdlib + available libs.
- No OCR improvements for PDF (keep existing).
- No frontend redesign; only widen format hints if needed.
- No semantic/embedding-based chunking (would need embedder at parse time); keep structural + token approach, add sentence boundaries.

## Constraints
- Read-only until Gate B. Tests: uv run pytest tests/ -q. Typecheck: uv run mypy services/ --ignore-missing-imports. Lint: uv run ruff check services/.
- Manifest version bump triggers reindex on boot (acceptable).

| Option | Effort | Risk | Blast radius | Reversibility |

| A: Minimal - add csv/json/code parsers only, leave chunker | Low | Low | Small | High |
| B: Hybrid - parsers + chunker improvements + registry (recommended) | Med | Med | Medium | Med |
| C: Full rewrite with unstructured library | High | High | Large | Low |

"""CSV/TSV parser: turn delimited rows into table blocks."""

import csv
import io

from packages.core.models import DocumentFormat
from services.ingestion.parsers.base import Block, ParsedDocument


def parse_csv(content: str, title: str = "") -> ParsedDocument:
    normalized = content.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(normalized))
    rows = [row for row in reader if any(cell.strip() for cell in row)]
    if not rows:
        return ParsedDocument(title=title or "Untitled document", format=DocumentFormat.CSV, blocks=[])

    blocks: list[Block] = []
    # First row as header.
    header = rows[0]
    blocks.append(Block(kind="table", text=" | ".join(cell.strip() for cell in header)))

    # Group data rows into chunks of ~20 rows to keep tables manageable.
    group_size = 20
    data_rows = rows[1:]
    for start in range(0, len(data_rows), group_size):
        group = data_rows[start : start + group_size]
        lines = [" | ".join(cell.strip() for cell in row) for row in group]
        blocks.append(Block(kind="table", text="\n".join(lines)))

    resolved_title = title or "Untitled document"
    # Try to derive a title from a 'title' or 'name' column.
    for idx, cell in enumerate(header):
        if cell.strip().lower() in ("title", "name", "document"):
            if len(rows) > 1 and idx < len(rows[1]):
                resolved_title = rows[1][idx].strip() or resolved_title
            break

    return ParsedDocument(title=resolved_title, format=DocumentFormat.CSV, blocks=blocks)

"""Code parser: language-aware structural blocks (functions/classes) with fallback grouping."""

import re

from packages.core.models import DocumentFormat
from services.ingestion.parsers.base import Block, ParsedDocument

# Language -> (line comment, function/class patterns)
_LANGUAGE_PATTERNS = {
    "py": [
        re.compile(r"^(def |class )\w+"),
    ],
    "js": [
        re.compile(r"^(export\s+)?(async\s+)?function\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^(export\s+)?class\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^(export\s+)?const\s+\w+\s*=\s*(async\s*)?\("),
    ],
    "ts": None,
    "tsx": None,
    "java": [
        re.compile(r"^\s*(public|private|protected|static|\s)*\s*(class|interface|enum)\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^\s*(public|private|protected|static|\s)*\s*\w+\s+\w+\s*\("),
    ],
    "go": [
        re.compile(r"^func\s+"),
        re.compile(r"^type\s+\w+\s+struct"),
    ],
    "rs": [
        re.compile(r"^(pub\s+)?(async\s+)?fn\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^(pub\s+)?struct\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^(pub\s+)?enum\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^(pub\s+)?trait\s+\w+"),
    ],
    "c": None,
    "cpp": None,
    "rb": [
        re.compile(r"^def\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^class\s+\w+"),
        re.compile(r"^module\s+\w+"),
    ],
    "sh": None,
    "bash": None,
}

_FALLBACK_GROUP = 60


def _patterns_for(language: str):
    pats = _LANGUAGE_PATTERNS.get(language.lower())
    if pats is None:
        # Generic: top-level def/class/function
        return [
            re.compile(r"^(def |class |function |func |fn )\w+"),
        ]
    return pats


def parse_code(content: str, title: str = "", language: str = "text") -> ParsedDocument:
    lines = content.splitlines()
    blocks: list[Block] = []
    patterns = _patterns_for(language)

    # Find boundary line indices where a new top-level definition starts.
    boundaries: list[int] = []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.lstrip()
        if not stripped or line.startswith((" ", "\t")):
            continue
        if any(p.match(stripped) for p in patterns):
            boundaries.append(index)

    if not boundaries:
        # Fallback: group lines.
        for start in range(0, len(lines), _FALLBACK_GROUP):
            chunk_lines = lines[start : start + _FALLBACK_GROUP]
            text = "\n".join(chunk_lines).strip()
            if text:
                blocks.append(Block(kind="code", text=text))
        if not blocks and content.strip():
            blocks.append(Block(kind="code", text=content.strip()))
        return ParsedDocument(
            title=title or "Untitled document", format=DocumentFormat.CODE, blocks=blocks
        )

    # Slice from each boundary to the next.
    boundaries.append(len(lines))
    for i in range(len(boundaries) - 1):
        start = boundaries[i]
        end = boundaries[i + 1]
        # include leading blanks? keep tight
        text = "\n".join(lines[start:end]).strip()
        if text:
            blocks.append(Block(kind="code", text=text))

    if not blocks and content.strip():
        blocks.append(Block(kind="code", text=content.strip()))

    resolved_title = title or "Untitled document"
    # Try to derive title from first function/class name.
    for line in lines:
        m = re.match(r"^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:def|class|function|func|fn|type)\s+(\w+)", line)
        if m:
            resolved_title = m.group(1)
            break

    return ParsedDocument(title=resolved_title, format=DocumentFormat.CODE, blocks=blocks)

def _split_oversized(self, block) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
        units = _split_units(block.text, block.kind)
        pieces: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
        piece_budget = max(
            1,
            min(
                self.target_tokens, self.max_tokens - min(self.overlap_tokens, self.max_tokens - 1)
            ),
        )
        current: list[str] = []
        current_tokens = 0
        for unit in units:
            if unit.tokens > self.max_tokens:
                # A single unit (very long sentence/row/line) is hard-split by words.
                if current:
                    pieces.append(("\n".join(current), current_tokens))
                    current, current_tokens = [], 0
                words = unit.text.split()
                window: list[str] = []
                window_tokens = 0
                for word in words:
                    cost = count_tokens(word)
                    if window and window_tokens + cost > piece_budget:
                        pieces.append((" ".join(window), window_tokens))
                        window, window_tokens = [], 0
                    window.append(word)
                    window_tokens += cost
                if window:
                    pieces.append((" ".join(window), window_tokens))
                continue
            if current_tokens + unit.tokens > piece_budget and current:
                pieces.append(("\n".join(current), current_tokens))
                current, current_tokens = [], 0
            current.append(unit.text)
            current_tokens += unit.tokens
        if current:
            pieces.append(("\n".join(current), current_tokens))
        return pieces

Improved RAG ingestion to accept common document formats (pdf, docx, md, txt, html, csv, json, code, yaml) via an extensible parser registry, and replaced naive space-split fallback with hybrid structure-aware + sentence-aware chunking. Added heuristic structure detection to plain text. Widened ingest API format regex. Added chunker params for new formats and format-aware legacy chunk() dispatch.
